reader.requirement: At --std 85 the END-PERFORM phrase ends an in-line PERFORM (formats 1-4 with procedure-name-1 omitted): each END-PERFORM closes the most recent unterminated in-line PERFORM, the statements between are its specified set, an in-line PERFORM without END-PERFORM or with an empty body is refused, END-PERFORM after an out-of-line PERFORM is refused (SR1), and an unterminated conditional statement before END-PERFORM is refused because imperative-statement-1 must be imperative.

edition-consulted.switches: bare LOCATION as a Format-3 head only at 2023 (is2023 predicate); at 85 PERFORM LOCATION is an out-of-line PERFORM
the Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM (WHEN phrases before END-PERFORM) is refused below 2023 with COBOL0900
an AFTER phrase in an in-line PERFORM is refused below 2002 (1985 SR2)

reader.edition-search: grep of CobolControlFlow.g4 for is2023/edition predicates, VersionConformancePass for Perform visitors, ProcedureFormatPass and CobolErrorStrategy for Edition/Year: the scope delimitation itself (grammar alternative ending in END_PERFORM, statementBlock) is edition-blind
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: END-PERFORM delimits the in-line PERFORM identically; only which in-line heads are admitted (AFTER from 2002, WHEN/LOCATION in 2023) differs, and 85 refuses those
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise IF/END-IF scope and a VARYING brace group; nested in-line PERFORMs, in-line PERFORM inside IF/ELSE, missing END-PERFORM, empty body, END-PERFORM after an out-of-line PERFORM and an unterminated conditional before END-PERFORM were not exercised

probes.printed: OUTER 1 N=03 / OUTER 2 N=06 / AFTER N=06 / T / T / THEN-TAIL / IF-DONE / TA N=03 / IN-IF / IN-IF (MATCH)
probes.expected: each END-PERFORM ends the nearest unterminated in-line PERFORM; the ELSE belongs to the IF
refused: an in-line PERFORM needs END-PERFORM (SR1, GR5)

probes.printed: COBOL0306 END-PERFORM appears without a matching PERFORM statement
probes.expected: refused: SR1, END-PERFORM must not follow an out-of-line PERFORM

reader.notes: The in-line PERFORM is one grammar alternative closed by END_PERFORM, so nesting pairs by the parse; refusals come from the grammar, the error strategy and ProcedureFormatPass, none edition-dependent. Diagnosis quality only: p5b (missing END-PERFORM) is reported as COBOL2269 'The ADD statement ends before this token' at the period, which does not name END-PERFORM; identical at --std 2023. The program is refused as the rule requires.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR5, VI.6.21.3 SR1 and IV.6.4.3 (same-verb nesting applies only between delimited scope statements, so an out-of-line PERFORM inside an in-line one must not take the END-PERFORM). Probes (refute-1985-111): q5a MATCH: out-of-line PERFORM P-X / P-X 2 TIMES / P-X THRU P-Y UNTIL / P-X VARYING inside an identifier-TIMES in-line PERFORM, END-PERFORM closes the in-line one (A N=65); in-line PERFORM inside a SEARCH WHEN; three-level nesting VARYING an index-name / TIMES / TEST AFTER (C N=28); comma and semicolon separators around END-PERFORM. q5d: a second END-PERFORM refused COBOL0306. q5b/q5c (class c, later-edition form): EXIT PERFORM and EXIT PERFORM CYCLE inside an in-line PERFORM refused COBOL0900 'requires COBOL-2002'. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VI.6.21.4 GR5 ... the text is in GR5'; 'OK  §1985:VI.6.21.3 SR1 ... the text is in SR1'; 'OK  §1985:IV.6.4.3 ... the text is in the clause'.
